466	/-! ## §5. What `[κ(P):k] = 1` actually says
467	
468	Both the uniform generation statement (`r = 1`) and the open geometric leaf
469	`Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero` (through
470	`degree_principal_eq_zero_of_residueDeg_eq_one`, `SectionBounds.lean` §4) reduce to the
471	single fact `residueDeg k P = 1`.  It has been carried as an informal remark — "over an
472	algebraically closed base every closed point has residue field `k̄`".  This section
473	replaces the remark by a **machine-checked equivalence** to a concrete, checkable
474	statement about rational functions:
475	
476	`residueDeg k P = 1 ↔ every function of order ≥ 0 at `P` agrees with a constant to
477	first order at `P`.`
478	
479	That is `residueDeg_eq_one_iff_hasRationalResidues`.  It converts the remaining leaf from
480	a claim about residue fields — which in this substrate would require identifying
481	`localStepTgt k P 1` with `IsLocalRing.ResidueField (X.presheaf.stalk P.point)`, an
482	identification this project does not have — into an approximation statement in the order
483	language the substrate already speaks.
484	
485	Note what is **not** claimed *in this section*: `HasRationalResidues` is not proved here for
486	an algebraically closed base.  Doing so needs the multiplicative structure of `κ(P)` (a
487	finite-dimensional *field* extension of an algebraically closed `k` is trivial —
488	`IsAlgClosed.algebraMap_bijective_of_isIntegral`), and `localStepTgt k P 1` is
489	constructed here as a quotient of `k`-submodules with no ring structure on it.  Finite
490	dimensionality alone does not give dimension one for a mere vector space, so the gap is
491	real and is exactly the missing ring-structure identification.
492	
493	**It is proved elsewhere now**, for a curve: `Adelic.hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed_curve`
494	(`Adelic/ResidueField.lean`).  Note how it escapes the obstruction just described — it never
495	identifies `localStepTgt k P 1` with the stalk residue field.  It proves the *approximation
496	statement* directly, by lifting to the stalk and using that `k → κ_P` is onto there, and then
497	feeds it back through this section's equivalence to reach `residueDeg k P = 1`.  So the `iff`
498	above is what makes the discharge possible: the ring-structure identification is still absent,
499	and is still not needed.
500	-/
501	
502	section RationalResidues
503	
504	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
505	    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
506	    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X]
507	
508	/-- **Every function regular at `P` agrees with a constant to first order.**
509	`∀ f` with `ord_P f ≥ 0`, some `c ∈ k` has `ord_P (f − c) ≥ 1`.
510	
511	This is the concrete content of "`κ(P) = k`", phrased in the order language rather than
512	through the residue field: the residue of `f` at `P` is the constant `c`.  Over an
513	algebraically closed base field it is the standard fact that a closed point of a curve
514	has residue field the base field; here it is an explicit hypothesis, and
515	`residueDeg_eq_one_iff_hasRationalResidues` shows it is *exactly* equivalent to
516	`[κ(P):k] = 1`. -/
517	def HasRationalResidues (P : X.PrimeDivisor) : Prop :=
518	  ∀ f : X.functionField, f ∈ orderGe P 0 →
519	    ∃ c : k, f - algebraMap k X.functionField c ∈ orderGe P 1
520	
521	/-- **`[κ(P):k] = 1` is equivalent to first-order approximation by constants.**
522	
523	`→` The quotient `localStepTgt k P 1 = orderGe P 0 / orderGe P 1` has dimension one and
524	its class of `1` is nonzero (`nontrivial_localStepTgt_one`), hence spans; so the class of
525	any `f` is `c • [1] = [c]`, i.e. `f − c ∈ orderGe P 1`.
526	
527	`←` Conversely, approximation says every class is a `k`-multiple of `[1]`, so the
528	quotient is spanned by one vector and has dimension `≤ 1`; with `1 ≤ [κ(P):k]`
529	(`one_le_residueDeg`) it is exactly `1`.
530	
531	The `→` direction needs no finiteness instance; `←` produces one, since a space spanned
532	by a single vector is finite-dimensional. -/
533	theorem residueDeg_eq_one_iff_hasRationalResidues (P : X.PrimeDivisor)
534	    [Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)] :
535	    residueDeg k P = 1 ↔ HasRationalResidues k P := by
536	  have hone : (1 : X.functionField) ∈ orderGeSub k P (1 - 1) := by
537	    rw [mem_orderGeSub]
538	    exact Or.inr (by rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_one]; norm_num)
539	  constructor
540	  · -- dimension one: the class of `1` spans
541	    intro hdeg f hf
542	    -- `[1] ≠ 0`, and in a 1-dimensional space a nonzero vector spans
543	    have hspan : ∀ z : localStepTgt k P 1, ∃ c : k,
544	        z = c • Submodule.Quotient.mk (p := Submodule.comap
545	          (orderGeSub k P (1 - 1)).subtype (orderGeSub k P 1)) ⟨1, hone⟩ := by
546	      intro z
547	      haveI := nontrivial_localStepTgt_one k P
548	      have hne : Submodule.Quotient.mk (p := Submodule.comap
549	          (orderGeSub k P (1 - 1)).subtype (orderGeSub k P 1))
550	          (⟨1, hone⟩ : orderGeSub k P (1 - 1)) ≠ 0 := by
551	        intro h
552	        rw [Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero, Submodule.mem_comap, Submodule.subtype_apply,
553	          mem_orderGeSub] at h
554	        rcases h with h0 | h0
555	        · exact one_ne_zero h0
556	        · rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_one] at h0; norm_num at h0
557	      -- a nonzero vector in a space of rank 1 spans it
558	      have hfr : Module.finrank k (localStepTgt k P 1) = 1 := hdeg
559	      obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := (finrank_eq_one_iff_of_nonzero' _ hne).mp hfr z
560	      exact ⟨c, hc.symm⟩
561	    obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := hspan (Submodule.Quotient.mk
562	      (p := Submodule.comap (orderGeSub k P (1 - 1)).subtype (orderGeSub k P 1))
563	      ⟨f, (mem_orderGeSub k).mpr hf⟩)
564	    refine ⟨c, ?_⟩
565	    -- unwind `[f] = c • [1]` into `f - c ∈ orderGe P 1`
566	    rw [← Submodule.Quotient.mk_smul, Submodule.Quotient.eq, Submodule.mem_comap,
567	      Submodule.subtype_apply] at hc
568	    rw [mem_orderGeSub] at hc
569	    have : ((⟨f, (mem_orderGeSub k).mpr hf⟩ : orderGeSub k P (1 - 1)) -
570	        c • ⟨1, hone⟩ : orderGeSub k P (1 - 1)) =
571	        (⟨f - algebraMap k X.functionField c, by
572	          have h1 : algebraMap k X.functionField c ∈ orderGeSub k P (1 - 1) := by
573	            have := (orderGeSub k P (1 - 1)).smul_mem c hone
574	            rwa [Algebra.smul_def, mul_one] at this
575	          exact (orderGeSub k P (1 - 1)).sub_mem ((mem_orderGeSub k).mpr hf) h1⟩ :
576	          orderGeSub k P (1 - 1)) := by
577	      apply Subtype.ext
578	      change f - c • (1 : X.functionField) = f - algebraMap k X.functionField c
579	      rw [Algebra.smul_def, mul_one]
580	    rw [this] at hc
581	    exact hc
582	  · -- approximation: the class of `1` spans, so the rank is at most one
583	    intro happrox
584	    have hle : residueDeg k P ≤ 1 := by
585	      rw [residueDeg]
586	      -- the quotient is spanned by the single class of `1`
587	      have hspan : (⊤ : Submodule k (localStepTgt k P 1)) ≤
588	          Submodule.span k {Submodule.Quotient.mk (p := Submodule.comap
589	            (orderGeSub k P (1 - 1)).subtype (orderGeSub k P 1)) ⟨1, hone⟩} := by
590	        intro z _
591	        obtain ⟨g, rfl⟩ := Submodule.Quotient.mk_surjective _ z
592	        obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := happrox (g : X.functionField)
593	          (by
594	            have hg2 := g.2
595	            rw [mem_orderGeSub] at hg2
596	            exact orderGe_antitone (by norm_num) hg2)
597	        rw [Submodule.mem_span_singleton]
598	        refine ⟨c, ?_⟩
599	        rw [← Submodule.Quotient.mk_smul, Submodule.Quotient.eq, Submodule.mem_comap,
600	          Submodule.subtype_apply]
601	        have hval : ((c • ⟨1, hone⟩ - g : orderGeSub k P (1 - 1)) :
602	            X.functionField) = -(g - algebraMap k X.functionField c) := by
603	          change c • (1 : X.functionField) - (g : X.functionField) = _
604	          rw [Algebra.smul_def, mul_one]
605	          ring
606	        rw [mem_orderGeSub, hval]
607	        exact (orderGe P 1).neg_mem hc
608	      have := Submodule.finrank_mono hspan
609	      rw [finrank_top] at this
610	      refine this.trans ?_
611	      rcases eq_or_ne (Submodule.Quotient.mk (p := Submodule.comap
612	          (orderGeSub k P (1 - 1)).subtype (orderGeSub k P 1))
613	          (⟨1, hone⟩ : orderGeSub k P (1 - 1))) 0 with h0 | h0
614	      · rw [h0, Submodule.span_zero_singleton, finrank_bot]; norm_num
615	      · rw [finrank_span_singleton h0]

621	/-! ## §6. The rational-residue case: `r = 1` and the unweighted degree
622	
623	Under `HasRationalResidues` at every prime divisor — the substrate's form of "the base
624	field is algebraically closed" — the two hypotheses that §4 and `SectionBounds.lean` §4
625	left open both become discharged simultaneously, because both were the same fact:
626	
627	* the uniform generation bound gets `r = 1`, so the threshold is `b + 1`;
628	* `deg_k = deg` (`degK_eq_degree_of_residueDeg_eq_one`), so the weighted statements
629	  become statements about the geometric degree — in particular the principal-degree-zero
630	  leaf.
631	
632	This is the precise pay-off of §5: one approximation hypothesis, two consequences.
633	-/
634	
635	section RationalResidueConsequences
636	
637	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
638	    [IsNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
639	    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X] (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)
640	
641	/-- **Rational residues everywhere give residue degree one everywhere.** -/
642	theorem residueDeg_eq_one_of_hasRationalResidues
643	    (hres : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, HasRationalResidues k P)
644	    [∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)]
645	    (P : X.PrimeDivisor) : residueDeg k P = 1 :=
646	  (residueDeg_eq_one_iff_hasRationalResidues k P).mpr (hres P)
647	
648	/-- **Uniform global generation with threshold `b + 1`.**  With rational residues at
649	every point, the residue-degree bound of `exists_bound_forall_generatedAt` is `r = 1`, so
650	one threshold works for every point and the shift over the vanishing bound is a single
651	unit.
652	
653	This is the classical shape: above `deg D ≥ b + 1`, `𝒪(D)` is generated by global
654	sections everywhere.  It remains single-field. -/
655	theorem exists_bound_forall_generatedAt_of_hasRationalResidues
656	    (hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
657	    (D₀ : X.WeilDivisor) (hbase : Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D₀))
658	    (hpeel : ∀ D' : X.WeilDivisor,
659	      (∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D₀) P ≤
660	        (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P) →
661	      Peel k U₀ U₁ D₀ D')
662	    (hres : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, HasRationalResidues k P)
663	    [∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k ⊤ D)]
664	    [∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)] :
665	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, b ≤ degK k D →
666	      ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, GeneratedAt k D P :=
667	  exists_bound_forall_generatedAt k U₀ U₁ hledger D₀ hbase hpeel 1
668	    (fun P => le_of_eq (residueDeg_eq_one_of_hasRationalResidues k hres P))
669	
670	/-- **The weighted degree is the geometric degree, under rational residues.**  Together
671	with `degK_principal_eq_zero` this is the unweighted principal-degree-zero statement; see
672	`degree_principal_eq_zero_of_residueDeg_eq_one` (`SectionBounds.lean`), whose residue
673	hypothesis is now reduced to `HasRationalResidues`. -/
674	theorem degK_eq_degree_of_hasRationalResidues
675	    (hres : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, HasRationalResidues k P)
676	    [∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)]
677	    (D : X.WeilDivisor) : degK k D = Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree D :=
678	  degK_eq_degree_of_residueDeg_eq_one k
679	    (fun P _ => residueDeg_eq_one_of_hasRationalResidues k hres P)

/-
Axiom-frontier probe.  Not part of the library: run it with

    lake env lean scripts/axiom-frontier.lean

from the project root.  Every `#print axioms` line below reports the axioms a
declaration actually depends on, `sorryAx` included, so a declaration that is
locally `sorry`-free but consumes a `sorry`-bodied *instance* through typeclass
synthesis is exposed here and nowhere else.

What this probe does NOT establish is at least as important as what it does, so read
§6b, §6c and §8 before quoting any "clean" line as a completeness claim.  A clean axiom
set means one thing only: no `sorry` is reachable from that proof term.  It says nothing
about unproved or even false hypotheses carried in the statement.

Companion measurement — reachability of the headline.  `#print axioms` says what
the headline depends on; the import graph says what it *could* depend on.  A
headline importing only `Genus.lean` cannot rest on the Picard, cohomology or
Riemann-Roch work no matter what its docstring claims, so the size of its
transitive project-import closure is the honest check that the infrastructure is
wired to the stated theorem:

    python3 - <<'PY'
    import os, re
    def imports(m):
        p = m.replace('.', '/') + '.lean'
        return re.findall(r'^import\s+(AlgebraicJacobian[\w.]*)', open(p).read(), re.M) \
               if os.path.exists(p) else []
    seen, stack = set(), ['AlgebraicJacobian.Jacobian']
    while stack:
        m = stack.pop()
        if m not in seen:
            seen.add(m); stack += imports(m)
    total = sum(1 for _, _, fs in os.walk('AlgebraicJacobian') for f in fs
                if f.endswith('.lean'))
    print(f'{len(seen)} of {total} project modules reachable from the headline')

8 before `picardJacobianWitness` was wired to `Scheme.Pic0Scheme`.  The two most recent

integrality, and `Albanese/AlbaneseUP.lean`, which the headline now reaches because leaf C

open RingHom

variable (n m : ℕ) {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)

/-- A morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y` is smooth if for each affine `U ⊆ Y` and
`V ⊆ f ⁻¹' U`, The induced map `Γ(Y, U) ⟶ Γ(X, V)` is smooth. -/
@[mk_iff]
class Smooth (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop where
  smooth_appLE (f) :
    ∀ {U : Y.Opens} (_ : IsAffineOpen U) {V : X.Opens} (_ : IsAffineOpen V) (e : V ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U),
      (f.appLE U V e).hom.Smooth

alias Scheme.Hom.smooth_appLE := Smooth.smooth_appLE

@[deprecated (since := "2026-02-09")] alias IsSmooth := Smooth

/-- The property of scheme morphisms `Smooth` is associated with the ring
homomorphism property `Smooth`. -/
instance : HasRingHomProperty @Smooth RingHom.Smooth where
  isLocal_ringHomProperty := RingHom.Smooth.propertyIsLocal
  eq_affineLocally' := by
    ext X Y f
    rw [smooth_iff, affineLocally_iff_forall_isAffineOpen]

/--
A morphism of schemes is smooth if and only if for each `x : X` there exists an affine open
exists an affine open neighborhood `V` of `x` and an affine open neighborhood `U` of
`f.base x` with `V ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U` such that the induced map `Γ(Y, U) ⟶ Γ(X, V)` is
standard smooth of relative dimension `n`.
-/
@[mk_iff]
class SmoothOfRelativeDimension : Prop where
  exists_isStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension : ∀ (x : X), ∃ (U : Y.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen U)
    (V : X.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen V) (_ : x ∈ V) (e : V ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U),
    IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension n (f.appLE U V e).hom

@[deprecated (since := "2026-02-09")] alias IsSmoothOfRelativeDimension := SmoothOfRelativeDimension

/-- If `f` is smooth of any relative dimension, it is smooth. -/
lemma SmoothOfRelativeDimension.smooth [SmoothOfRelativeDimension n f] : Smooth f := by
  rw [Smooth.iff_forall_exists_isStandardSmooth]
  intro x
  obtain ⟨U, hU, V, hV, hx, e, hf⟩ := exists_isStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension (n := n) (f := f) x
  exact ⟨U, hU, V, hV, hx, e, hf.isStandardSmooth⟩
